identity.headline: I break binaries for a living — and write down exactly how.
identity.subline: Reverse engineering, malware analysis and SOC automation. Solo-built an 8-stage nested-VM malware pipeline; ENIT placed 77th globally at HTB University CTF 2025.

availability.text: Available for a 6-month internship from February 2027

about.bio: I'm a cybersecurity-focused ICT Engineering student at ENIT with a bias toward the hard parts of the stack: unpacking .NET obfuscation, emulating shellcode, tracing syscalls in a live VM, and turning the result into an automated pipeline. I built an 8-stage nested-VM malware analysis pipeline end to end as a sole-contributor research intern — static triage through eBPF syscall tracing, Volatility3 VMI correlation, anti-sandbox evasion, C2 sinkholing and automated MITRE ATT&CK attribution. I also work in ML for security: graph neural networks over binary control-flow graphs, and reinforcement learning for autonomous intrusion response. I compete in CTFs with SECURINETS ENIT and contribute to open-source security tooling through G2FOSS.

bullets: Architected an 8-stage automated malware analysis pipeline: static triage → de4dot deobfuscation → Speakeasy emulation → live QEMU-KVM detonation → eBPF syscall capture → Volatility3 VMI correlation → MITRE ATT&CK mapping → automated PDF reporting.

Correlated host-side eBPF KVM tracepoints with Volatility3 VMI on a live guest, and patched KUSER_SHARED_DATA.TickCount in guest memory to defeat anti-sandbox timing checks. Validated against live AsyncRAT, AgentTesla and njRAT samples.
Deployed a multi-layer C2 sinkhole (iptables + DNSChef + INetSim) to capture malware traffic and extract actionable IOCs with false-positive filtering against Windows telemetry.
Automated threat attribution by matching IOCs against VirusTotal, AlienVault OTX and MalwareBazaar, grouping behavioural families with MinHash LSH clustering and generating PDF reports automatically.
Triaged 15+ daily technical support tickets and provisioned network modems at scale, cutting average per-unit configuration time by 20% through scripted workflows.
Maintained network uptime across multiple customer sites.

projects.name: Nested-VM Malware Analysis Pipeline
projects.desc: An end-to-end 8-stage automated malware analysis pipeline. QEMU/KVM live detonation with host-side eBPF syscall tracing correlated against Volatility3 VMI, anti-sandbox evasion via KUSER_SHARED_DATA patching in guest memory, multi-layer C2 sinkholing with DNSChef + INetSim + iptables, and automated MITRE ATT&CK attribution with MinHash LSH clustering. Validated against live AsyncRAT, AgentTesla and njRAT samples.

projects.name: CFG Function Localization via Graph Neural Networks
projects.desc: Stripped ELF/PE binaries disassembled with headless Ghidra and angr, then mapped into directed control-flow graphs whose node features are x86/ARM opcode distributions and API call references. GCNs and GATs (PyTorch Geometric) are trained for node-level classification of malicious functions — anti-debug loops, keyloggers and process-injection routines.

projects.name: RL-Based Intrusion Detection & Response
projects.desc: Network defense formulated as an MDP with six response actions (DPI, throttle, honeypot, block, isolate, quarantine) inside a custom Gymnasium environment. A Double DQN agent with prioritized experience replay is trained on CSE-CIC-IDS2018 telemetry to choose response actions instead of only raising alerts.

projects.name: Open-Source SOC Automation
projects.desc: A Wazuh SIEM + Shuffle SOAR lab deployed automatically with Ansible and Docker. A Python suppression microservice filters 33,022 noisy events down to a single actionable incident — over 95% noise reduction — with a human-in-the-loop VirusTotal enrichment pipeline and custom detection rules validated against simulated brute force, lateral movement and privilege escalation.

projects.name: Wi-Fi Security Research
projects.desc: Demonstrated WPA2 and ARP-spoofing weaknesses with Wireshark and Bettercap in an isolated lab. Documented the MITM attack chain end to end and proposed concrete mitigations: 802.1X, HSTS enforcement and certificate pinning.

projects.name: Village Under Attack — C++ Strategy Game
projects.desc: A real-time terminal strategy game in C++ built on OOP principles, non-blocking I/O, NPC pathfinding and collision detection. Systems programming and algorithmic design outside a security context — the discipline that makes the reversing work easier.

projects.name: Embedded Face Recognition & Hardware Automation
projects.desc: A real-time facial recognition pipeline in Python/OpenCV driving an Arduino microcontroller over UART. Identity verification triggers a physical hardware action, demonstrating secure serial protocol design and embedded security.
